Flooding Disrupts Metals & Mining Operations in Cayman Islands

GEORGE TOWN, Cayman Islands, June 24 — Widespread flooding triggered by days of torrential rain has forced the suspension of operations at several metals and mining sites across the Cayman Islands, with companies warning of potential delays to shipments and production losses.

Chinalco Mining Corp International said Monday it had halted processing at its main bauxite facility near Bodden Town after floodwaters swamped access roads and power was temporarily cut to key infrastructure. “Our immediate priority is ensuring the safety of personnel and protecting equipment from water damage. We are assessing the extent of the disruption and will update our customers as soon as possible,” a company spokesperson said.

The Cayman Islands Mining Association reported that at least four major sites have experienced flooding or logistical bottlenecks as swollen rivers and submerged roadways hampered the movement of ore and refined metals to the port in George Town. “Transport links are severely compromised, making it difficult for trucks to reach export terminals,” association president Thomas Ebanks said.

Local authorities have issued flood warnings for low-lying areas, with meteorologists forecasting more rain over the next 48 hours. The National Emergency Operations Centre said teams are working to restore road access and assist stranded workers. No injuries have been reported among mining staff.

Industry analysts estimate that the flooding could disrupt the export of several thousand tonnes of alumina and nickel ore in the coming week if conditions persist. “This is the worst weather-related interruption the sector has faced here in over a decade,” said Rosanne Lee, an independent mining analyst based in the Cayman Islands.

Another affected operator, Caribbean Metals Ltd, said it was monitoring water levels at its Prospect Ridge plant and preparing to suspend operations if conditions worsen.

The full impact on production and exports remains uncertain as the flooding continues.
